subject: Tenant throttles, egress shaping & warmup matrix for private GPU deployment
messages:
From: Chris Morales <chris@ember.health>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 29 May 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial traffic samples & asks for tenant-level throttles

Hi Hannah / Jonas,

Thanks again for walking through the private deployment options yesterday. Attached are three anonymized sample traces from our staging deployment (ember-traffic-samples.csv). They include a 48-hour window with a mix of short conversational requests (avg 40 tokens) and heavier document-summarization jobs (avg 800 tokens).

Primary asks:
- We need an approach to limit noisy tenants without impacting latency for normal tenants.
- Can you recommend per-tenant concurrency caps and per-tenant egress shaping that still meets our 99th percentile latency SLO (<=350ms for small requests) while allowing occasional large-batch jobs?
- We also want a warmup strategy so first-burst jobs don't suffer cold cache penalties.

Can your team propose a matrix of throttle settings (concurrency, tokens/s, warmup window) and a simple test we can run in our staging env to validate?

Thanks,
Chris Morales
Head of Cloud Ops, EmberHealth

Attachments: ember-traffic-samples.csv (CSV, 52KB)

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Chris Morales <chris@ember.health>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial traffic samples & asks for tenant-level throttles

Chris — good dataset, thanks. I sketched a draft warmup + throttle matrix and a concrete test plan (attached). High level proposal:

1) Per-tenant concurrency caps (soft limits + burst token)
   - Small-tenants (<=100 qps steady): soft concurrency 16, burst token 8, cooldown 30s
   - Mid-tenants (100-1k qps): soft concurrency 48, burst token 24, cooldown 90s
   - Large tenants (>1k qps): soft concurrency 128, burst token 64, cooldown 300s

Rationale: soft limits throttle admission early to protect KV cache locality and GPU lane saturation; burst tokens allow short spikes for priority background jobs.

2) Egress shaping by token-rate window (tokens/s) tied to model profile
   - Conversational model: 1500 tokens/s per tenant ceiling, steady alpha=0.75 smoothing over 10s
   - Long-form model: 600 tokens/s per tenant ceiling, smoothing over 30s

3) Progressive warmup windows (cache-priming + admission ramp)
   - Probe phase (30s): low-rate probe requests for cache priming (1-2 qps per worker)
   - Ramp phase (2–5 min): increase concurrency in geometric steps (x1, x2, x4) while measuring 95/99 latency and token generation RPS
   - Stabilize phase: drop back to soft concurrency if 99th latency > target for two consecutive windows

4) Admission controller LUT & fallback policy
   - Maintain a small look-up table per deployment with expected tokens/sec per model and effective GPU lanes required. If a tenant's allocation request would exceed headroom, redirect to lower-cost variant (quantized model) or queue with SLA-backed estimate.

5) Test plan (staging):
   - Run three blended workloads from your CSV simultaneously (small convo / mixed / long-form).
   - Inject a noisy tenant at 3x expected peak and verify: cache-priming reduces 95 -> 99 latency delta by >= 20% vs no-warmup; overall P99 small requests <= 350ms for non-noisy tenants.

I've attached warmup-matrix-v1.xlsx with the concrete numbers and a suggested CLI to run the load. Jonas — can you validate the LUT approach and add any networking/egress headroom numbers?

Hannah
Director, Field Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachments: warmup-matrix-v1.xlsx (Excel, 28KB)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Chris Morales <chris@ember.health>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 31 May 2027 08:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial traffic samples & asks for tenant-level throttles

+1 on Hannah's plan — a few operational constraints and numbers to make the staging test actionable.

Operational notes:
- Networking headroom: plan for 20% egress buffer per rack for KV cache scattering and pipelined token responses. For your staging cluster (8 GPUs), reserve ~2.5 Gbps headroom beyond expected traffic to allow for model weights fetch/replication during warmup.

- Admission LUT entries (example rows):
   model_id, seq_len95, tokens/sec_per_lane, lanes_needed_per_request
   gpt-medium, 512, 400, 1
   gpt-large, 1024, 150, 2

- Concurrency -> GPU lane mapping: budget 1 lane per 8 concurrent small requests; 1 lane per 3 mid requests; large batch jobs should be scheduled into dedicated lanes when possible.

- KV cache priming: run parallel priming probes across shards to avoid thundering herd; probes should be random-key lookups at low qps per shard during the Probe phase.

- Simulation: I ran a quick sim (attached sim-results-run1.log) using a traffic-runner seeded from your CSV. Results: with the proposed caps and a 2-min ramp, non-noisy tenants stayed within P99=320–360ms depending on traffic mix. Noisy tenant tail pushed mid-tenant P99 by ~12% when burst tokens were unlimited — so we need the burst token cooldown enforcement.

Next steps:
- Chris: if you can run the CLI I attached to the warmup-matrix and share cloudwatch-like traces (qps, p95/p99, token-rates) I will iterate the LUT for your exact model mixes.
- I’ll add a small admission-controller feature toggle so you can A/B test with and without egress shaping.

—Jonas
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

Attachments: sim-results-run1.log (log, 14KB)

Hannah / Jonas — really helpful, thanks. Agree to the three-phase warmup and the burst token cooldown. A couple of operational asks from our side:

- Can we get the admission-controller toggle as a feature flag so we can flip it per-deployment?
- We'll run the warmup matrix tests today in staging and send you the traces (qps, p95/p99, egress bytes/s). Expect to reproduce the noisy-tenant spike at ~3x peak.
- One procurement note: if the fallback to quantized model is used frequently we need a line item in the contract for supported quantized variants (we'll loop in procurement if that looks likely).

If the staging tests match Jonas' sim we can schedule a short pilot next week to validate on your dedicated private pool using a single tenant carveout.

Thanks,
Chris
Head of Cloud Ops, EmberHealth
